title: Family tree
summary: A two-parent UUID graph with ancestor traversal and descendant path counts.
requirements: Store a person's name and parents, and register child links.
Return reachable parents and descendant path counts by depth.
nonfunctional: Traversal cost depends on the paths explored; no latency target is specified.
constraints: Identify people by UUID; allow at most two parents.
Append identities once; see the scope note for replacement behavior.
invariants: Return ancestors as a set; count descendant paths, not unique people.
acceptance: Descendant traversal emits a count for each node reached before the strict depth bound.
environment: Rama stream topology core; ancestors and descendants-count query topologies
decisions: $$family-tree is keyed by person UUID and stores a set of child UUIDs.
tradeoffs: Two-parent links keep records bounded; path counts can grow exponentially with depth.
seam: Callers create the input graph and generate UUIDs.

write: route once for each parent field, including nil in this source
read: the ancestors query follows non-nil parent edges and collects IDs into a set
the descendants query expands child paths and sums counts by depth
flow.partition: Writes hash by person ID, then hash-route to each parent ID; the PState is keyed by person UUID. Queries hash each traversed ID before local state access. The source also writes a nil-key child set for absent parents; the public contract queries UUIDs only.

caveat: The ancestor generation filter is inclusive, so generation 0 returns immediate parents. Descendant traversal uses depth < generations and counts before expanding children; an isolated leaf with a positive bound returns {0 0}. Replacing a record does not remove child links under its former parents.

title: Collaborative document editor
summary: Transforms versioned text operations against edits a client has not seen.
requirements: Transform stale operations against intervening edits.
Return the text and accepted operation count.
nonfunctional: History remains stored; transform work grows with unseen operations.
constraints: Callers provide valid offsets and removal ranges.
invariants: Version counts transformed stored operations: a split removal can add two; a fully subsumed removal adds zero.
acceptance: A stale edit receives the history slice starting at its version.
environment: Rama stream topology core; doc+version query
decisions: $$docs stores current text; $$edits stores each document's edit vector.
tradeoffs: Colocation lets the module transform edits locally; retained history uses more storage and increases stale-edit cost.
seam: The reference does not define client coordination, history compaction, a UI, or an OT standard.

write: apply at the head or select unseen edits
store text and transformed edit vector
flow.partition: The depot and both document PStates key on Long document ID; the query hashes the same ID.

caveat: The challenge excludes insertions inside a removed span: the source transforms offset 3 against deletion [2,5) to offset 0. History is unbounded; crash/replay and performance are not verified.

title: Content moderation
summary: Recipient feeds with reader-specific author mutes and offset-based paging.
requirements: Mute or unmute authors for a reader.
Page through a feed without showing muted authors.
nonfunctional: Query work grows with scanned feed entries and mute lookups.
constraints: Offsets refer to the unfiltered feed.
invariants: Mutes apply from a reader to an author.
Unmuting restores access to historical posts.
acceptance: Pages preserve append order and scan past muted entries to fill the limit.
The next offset is nil at the end.
environment: Rama stream topology core; get-posts and helper query topologies
interfaces: ContentModeration protocol: post!, mute!, unmute!, get-posts
decisions: $$posts stores recipient vectors; $$mutes stores each reader's muted-author set.
tradeoffs: Recipient affinity keeps appends local. The query checks each post's author; long runs of muted posts increase query work.
seam: The reference does not include classification, post removal, ranking, reports, or a moderation queue.

write: route posts by recipient and append to the timeline
route mute/unmute by reader and change muted-author membership
read: continue to the limit or feed end
flow.partition: Post and mute depots and both PStates use their recipient/reader keys. The query partitions by reader; its helper reads colocated feed and mute state.

caveat: The adapter returns an empty page for offsets beyond feed end; this avoids an upstream srange exception. Ordinary pages use the unchanged query. Non-positive limits and fixed-work pagination are not promised.
